question.problem:
Written in the form $y=mx+b,$ what is the equation of the line that passes through the points  $(0,0)$ and $(2,-1)?$

The equation of the line is $y=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$ 

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-1-0}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{-1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The coordinates of the $y$-intercept are always $(0,b).$ We know that the line passes through the point $(0,0),$ so the $y$-intercept is $b=0.$

Substituting the slope $m=-\frac{1}{2}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=0$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=-\frac{1}{2}x+0=-\frac{1}{2}x.
$$
